messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: LR or AIC?
parts:
Samantha:

Your questions about model selection and goodness of fit are all good ones.  A good place to start to learn about these ideas is in Chapter 3 of Buckland et al. (2001): section 3.4 is about model choice.  In addition, you can have a look inside the Users Guide for Distance for more insight; in particular you can read a section in Chapter 8 (conventional distance sampling analysis) entitled CDS qq-plots to discuss these plots in the context of assessing fit of detection functions to data.

There are many other statistical references for the general topic of model selection, likelihood ratio, goodness of fit.  However the references above discuss them in the context of detection functions in distance sampling.

Do these two tests give the same results?
